abstract: ROR1 is a promising cancer target due to its tumor-specific expression. Here, we developed two high-affinity humanized anti-ROR1 antibodies (Hu001-2 and Hu005-46) targeting distinct epitopes, with Hu001-2 demonstrating blockade of Wnt5a-ROR1 signaling and rapid internalization. Based on Hu001-2, we generated an antibody-drug conjugate (Hu001-2-vcMMAE) that displayed potent ROR1-dependent anti-proliferative activity in vitro and significantly inhibited tumor growth across multiple ROR1-expressing in vivo models. Furthermore, we designed an antibody-cytokine fusion protein (Hu001-2-IL15Rα-IL15) that demonstrated potential anti-tumor activity in immunocompetent models. This fusion protein successfully activated the immune system within the tumor microenvironment, upregulating the expression of TNF-α and IFN-γ while exhibiting minimal systemic toxicity. Collectively, these novel Hu001-2-based therapeutics validated the feasibility of using the ROR1 fusion protein to trigger the activation of the immune system in the tumor microenvironment.
